transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi. Um, I came in today because... well, people have been pointing out how I'm moving lately. Like, they can actually see me either moving like I'm underwater—taking forever just to answer a question or even get out of a chair. Or else I'm doing the exact opposite. I'll just be pacing around my apartment and rubbing my hands together, kind of like I'm trying to shake off a bad call at work. It's just... it's really noticeable, I guess, so I figured I should talk to someone about it.
Have you ever experienced periods where your mood was extremely low or high, or where you felt unusually energetic or unable to sleep because your thoughts were racing?

Um, no, not really. I haven't noticed anything like that. I definitely don't get unusually energetic, and my thoughts don't race or keep me from sleeping. And I don't think my mood has been extremely high or low either. It's really just the physical moving stuff that I mentioned.
Have you ever experienced any unusual thoughts or perceptions, like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't, or believing something strongly that others find strange?

Well, I don't really have strange beliefs or see things, but... I guess I do hear things sometimes. It's usually work-related. Like, I'll hear the beep from my old headset, or a voice that sounds like a supervisor calling my name. Sometimes it just says "too slow." The weird thing is, it happens when my laptop is completely closed and there's definitely no phone ringing anywhere near me. It's pretty clear when it happens.
Do you hear these voices even when there’s no external sound or reminder of work around you?

Yeah, like I was just saying... it happens when there's absolutely nothing going on. My laptop will be completely shut, and there's no phone ringing anywhere near me. It can be totally quiet in my apartment, and I'll still clearly hear that headset beep, or the supervisor voice saying my name or telling me I'm too slow. So, yeah, it happens even without any real noise or work stuff open around me.

When you hear these voices, do they ever talk about what you're doing as you're doing it, like a running commentary, or do they sound like multiple voices talking to each other, or do they repeat your thoughts out loud as you think them?

No, it's nothing like that. They don't talk to each other or comment on what I'm doing. It's really just what I said before—just a quick beep, or a voice saying my name or "too slow." It's not like a whole conversation or anything repeating my thoughts. Just those short, work-related sounds.
Have you ever believed something strongly that other people don’t seem to agree with, even when there’s clear evidence against it?

Well, yeah, I guess there is one thing. Even when I’m having an okay week and feeling alright, I still get convinced that the ticketing software from my old job is somehow tracking me. Like, I really believe it's following me through different job search sites and secretly flagging me as unreliable to new employers. People tell me that's impossible and that the software doesn't work like that, but I just can't shake the feeling that it's happening.
Can you tell me more about how you know the ticketing software is tracking you, even though other people say it's not possible?

I mean, I don't have hard proof to show you. It's just... well, like I was saying, even when I’m having a pretty okay week and feeling fine, I still just get completely convinced that it's happening. I'll be looking at different job boards, and I just know that the ticketing software from my old job is somehow tracking me through those sites. It feels like it's running in the background and actively flagging me as unreliable to the new employers. My friends say the systems aren't connected like that and it's impossible, but I just can't shake the certainty that it's following me.
Even though others have told you it’s not possible, do you believe with absolute certainty that the ticketing software is tracking you, without any doubt at all?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I know I've said it a couple of times now, but even when I'm having an okay week and my mood is fine, I'm still just completely convinced it's happening. I don't have any doubt. I just know that the ticketing software from my old job is tracking me through those job sites and flagging me as unreliable to the places I'm applying to. People can tell me it's impossible all they want, but I know it's real.

Have you ever had the experience of feeling tracked or watched in other situations outside of job searching, or is this belief limited only to your experience with the ticketing software and job sites?

No, it's really just that one thing. Like I said, it doesn't matter if I'm having a decent week and feeling okay, I just get this overwhelming conviction that the old ticketing software is tracking me. It's just through the job sites, you know, flagging me as unreliable to the places I apply. I don't feel watched at the grocery store or in my apartment or anything like that. It's specifically just that software following me when I'm looking for work.
Even though people have given you reasons why it's not possible, do you feel like your belief that the ticketing software is tracking you is completely true and can't be questioned at all?

Yeah, I do. I know we keep going over it, but yes. Like I said, even if I'm having a totally okay week and my mood is fine, I still just get completely convinced that it's happening. I know the ticketing software from my old job is tracking me through those job sites and flagging me as unreliable. It doesn't matter what anyone else says about it, I know it's true.

Even though there’s no evidence that the ticketing software could track you, and people have explained that it’s not possible, do you still feel deep down that your belief is absolutely true and nothing could ever change your mind about it?

Yes. I mean, I know I keep repeating myself here, but yeah. Nothing is going to change my mind, because I know what's happening. Even if I'm having a pretty good week and my mood is totally fine, I still know it's true. That ticketing software from my old job is tracking me on those job sites, and it's flagging me as unreliable to the employers. I know people say it's impossible, but I know it's real.

Even though there’s no evidence that the ticketing software could track you, and people have explained that it’s not possible, do you still feel deep down that your belief is absolutely true and nothing could ever change your mind about it?

I feel like we're kind of going in circles here, but yes, my answer is still the same. Even when I'm having a perfectly okay week, I still get completely convinced that the ticketing software from my old job is somehow tracking me through those job sites. I just know it's flagging me as unreliable to the places I'm applying to. So, yeah, no matter what anyone else explains to me or how impossible they say it is, I still believe it's true.
